issue_description: A weakness has been identified in BYVoid OpenCC up to 1.1.9. This vulnerability affects the function opencc::MaxMatchSegmentation of the file src/MaxMatchSegmentation.cpp. This manipulation causes heap-based buffer overflow. The attack is restricted to local execution. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks. Patch name: 345c9a50ab07018f1b4439776bad78a0d40778ec. To fix this issue, it is recommended to deploy a patch.

A vulnerability has been found in janet-lang janet up to 1.40.1. The impacted element is the function janetc_pop_funcdef of the file src/core/compile.c. Such manipulation leads to out-of-bounds read. The attack must be carried out locally. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used. The name of the patch is 4dd08a4cdef5b1c42d9a2c19fc24412e97ef51d5. A patch should be applied to remediate this issue.

A vulnerability was found in janet-lang janet up to 1.40.1. This affects the function os_strftime of the file src/core/os.c. Performing a manipulation results in out-of-bounds read. The attack must be initiated from a local position. The exploit has been made public and could be used. The patch is named 0f285855f0e34f9183956be5f16e045f54626bff. To fix this issue, it is recommended to deploy a patch.

A vulnerability was determined in berry-lang berry up to 1.1.0. The affected element is the function scan_string of the file src/be_lexer.c. This manipulation causes out-of-bounds read. The attack requires local access. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized. Patch name: 7149c59a39ba44feca261b12f06089f265fec176. Applying a patch is the recommended action to fix this issue.

An issue was discovered in faad2 before 2.10.0. A heap-buffer-overflow exists in the function stszin located in mp4read.c. It allows an attacker to cause Code Execution.
Buffer overflow in the stbl_AppendSize function in MP4Box in GPAC 1.0.1 allows attackers to cause a denial of service or execute arbitrary code via a crafted file.

A Segmentation fault casued by heap use after free vulnerability exists in Gpac through 1.0.1 via the mpgviddmx_process function in reframe_mpgvid.c when using mp4box, which causes a denial of service.
Buffer Over-read in GitHub repository gpac/gpac prior to 2.1.0-DEV.

A vulnerability, which was classified as critical, has been found in GPAC 2.3-DEV-rev40-g3602a5ded. This issue affects the function mp3_dmx_process of the file filters/reframe_mp3.c. The manipulation leads to heap-based buffer overflow. The attack may be initiated remotely. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used. The associated identifier of this vulnerability is VDB-221087.

Buffer Overflow vulnerability in gpac MP4Box v.2.3-DEV-rev573-g201320819-master allows a local attacker to cause a denial of service via the gpac/src/isomedia/isom_read.c:2807:51 function in gf_isom_get_user_data.
GPAC v2.3-DEV-rev566-g50c2ab06f-master was discovered to contain a heap-use-after-free via the flush_ref_samples function at /gpac/src/isomedia/movie_fragments.c.
GPAC v2.3-DEV-rev566-g50c2ab06f-master was discovered to contain a double free via the gf_filterpacket_del function at /gpac/src/filter_core/filter.c.
Stack-based Buffer Overflow in GitHub repository gpac/gpac prior to 2.3-DEV.
Out-of-bounds Read in GitHub repository gpac/gpac prior to 2.3-DEV.

Heap-based buffer overflow in archive_string_append_from_wcs() (archive_string.c) in libarchive-3.4.1dev allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds write in heap memory resulting into a crash) via a crafted archive file. NOTE: this only affects users who downloaded the development code from GitHub. Users of the product's official releases are unaffected.
libdwarf 0.4.0 has a heap-based buffer over-read in _dwarf_check_string_valid in dwarf_util.c.
There is a heap-based buffer over-read in libdwarf 0.4.0. This issue is related to dwarf_global_formref_b.
libjpeg-turbo 2.0.4, and mozjpeg 4.0.0, has a heap-based buffer over-read in get_rgb_row() in rdppm.c via a malformed PPM input file.
Integer overflow vulnerability in Mat_VarReadNextInfo5 in mat5.c in tbeu matio (aka MAT File I/O Library) 1.5.17, allows attackers to cause a Denial of Service or possibly other unspecified impacts.
md_analyze_line in md4c.c in md4c 0.4.7 allows attackers to trigger use of uninitialized memory, and cause a denial of service via a malformed Markdown document.

A stack-based buffer overflow was discovered in the pgxtoimage function in bin/jp2/convert.c in OpenJPEG 2.2.0. The vulnerability causes an out-of-bounds write, which may lead to remote denial of service or possibly remote code execution.

libyara/grammar.y in YARA 3.5.0 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (use-after-free and application crash) via a crafted rule that is mishandled in the yr_parser_lookup_loop_variable function.
libyara/grammar.y in YARA 3.5.0 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (use-after-free and application crash) via a crafted rule that is mishandled in the yr_compiler_destroy function.

Stack-use-after-scope in xmlEscapeText (xmlIO.c): xmlEscapeText uses data from a stack-allocated temporary buffer after that buffer's lifetime ends, causing a read of stale stack memory (observed via a memcpy). This is reachable via node string handling / element validation (xmlNodeListGetStringInternal -> xmlValidateElement) and can lead to crashes or other memory-corruption impacts when parsing crafted XML.

A heap-buffer-overflow in libxml2's parser.c (xmlParsePubidLiteral) allows a one-byte out-of-bounds write when parsing PUBLIC identifiers (reachable via xmlParseExternalID/xmlParseDocTypeDecl). This out-of-bounds write can corrupt heap memory, causing crashes and potentially enabling arbitrary code execution when processing crafted DOCTYPE/external ID data.

Heap-use-after-free in libxml2: xmlValidateRef (src/valid.c) can dereference an xmlAttr/xmlRef pointer that has already been freed when using the validating XML reader. The validator walks the document's reference table and may read stale pointers to attributes removed by the reader, leading to a heap-use-after-free that can cause crashes or other memory-corruption impacts.

A heap-use-after-free in xinclude.c's xmlXIncludeIncludeNode (seen during xmlXIncludeDoProcess / xmlXIncludeProcessNode invoked from xmlTextReaderRead) reads memory from an XInclude node that has already been freed. This can lead to crashes, memory corruption, or potentially exploitable behavior when processing XInclude content.

Heap-use-after-free in xpath.c: xmlXPathNodeSetAdd (invoked via xmlXPathGetElementsByIds/xmlXPathIdFunction during XPath/XPointer evaluation) can access a node/attribute that was already freed while processing input (e.g. via xmlTextReader/XInclude). This results in reads of freed heap memory, leading to crashes and potential memory corruption when resolving ID-based references.

A bad-cast/UBSan error in parser.c's xmlParseElement causes a null pointer dereference (read from a near-zero address) when handling certain inputs. The invalid cast to an xmlStartTag-like structure leads to a segmentation fault and undefined behavior during parsing, which can be triggered by crafted XML and results in a denial-of-service crash.

An invalid-free in libxml2's parser (parser.c) causes xmlFreeNodeList/xmlFreeNode to attempt to free an address that was not obtained from malloc. The error occurs during reference/balanced-chunk parsing (xmlParseReference / xmlParseBalancedChunkMemoryInternal), leading to crashes and potential heap corruption when processing crafted XML (e.g., schema) inputs.

A use-of-uninitialized-value in htmlParseHTMLAttribute (HTMLparser.c) can cause an out-of-bounds read / global-buffer-overflow while parsing HTML attribute values. The parser may read past a local buffer into adjacent global memory, leading to crashes, incorrect behavior, or potential information disclosure.

A global-buffer-overflow (out-of-bounds read) occurs in xmlStrndup (xmlstring.c) when invoked from the HTML parser (HTMLparser.c) during DOCTYPE/system/public literal parsing (e.g., htmlParseSystemLiteral/htmlParseDocTypeDecl). The parser can supply an incorrect length/offset to xmlStrndup, causing it to read past the end of a buffer into adjacent global memory. This can crash the process and may lead to memory corruption or information disclosure.

Heap-use-after-free in htmlCurrentChar (HTMLparser.c): an encoding name buffer is freed while still referenced by the HTML error reporting path (htmlParseErr / __xmlRaiseError), causing subsequent formatted error output to read freed heap memory. This can lead to crashes (denial of service) and may be exploitable for arbitrary code execution depending on context.

A heap-use-after-free exists in libxml2's error reporting: xmlParserPrintFileContextInternal (error.c) can read from parser input pointers that reference freed heap memory when invoked via xmlReportError/__xmlRaiseError. This results in reads of deallocated memory during parsing (e.g., while handling entities or external subsets), leading to crashes or other undefined behavior and potentially enabling exploitation.

A global-buffer-overflow READ occurs in xmlDictHashName (dict.c), triggered during NCName/QName parsing (xmlParseNCName/xmlParseQNameHashed in parser.c). The hash/name lookup reads one byte out-of-bounds before the global table xmlIsPubidChar_tab (chvalid.c), which can lead to crashes or potential information disclosure when processing specially crafted XML names (e.g., element or attribute names).

Heap-use-after-free in libxml2: during entity/reference parsing (xmlParseReference in parser.c), xmlStaticCopyNode (tree.c) invoked via xmlDocCopyNode reads node/namespace data that has already been freed. This results in reads from freed heap memory, leading to crashes and potential memory-corruption-based exploitation.

Heap-use-after-free in libxml2's encoding cleanup: xmlCharEncCloseFunc (encoding.c) is invoked on an encoding handler that has already been freed during HTML output processing (htmlSaveFileFormat in HTMLtree.c / xmlOutputBufferClose in xmlIO.c). This leads to reads from freed heap memory, causing crashes or memory corruption and presenting a potential security risk when processing crafted HTML/XML input (e.g., via xmllint).

Heap-buffer-overflow in src/range.c (range_num_to_a): while converting numeric ranges to an array the function can write an 8-byte value past the end of the allocated array (out-of-bounds write). This corrupts heap memory and can lead to crashes or potential arbitrary code execution when handling certain numeric ranges (e.g., mixes of integers and floats).

mrb_str_format in mrbgems/mruby-sprintf/src/sprintf.c computes an incorrect (overflowed/negative) length when parsing numeric format specifiers, which can cause memcpy to be called with a negative size (ASAN "negative-size-param"). This leads to crashes and can result in out‑of‑bounds heap memory access or corruption, potentially enabling exploitation.

Heap-buffer-overflow in mrbgems/mruby-compiler/core/codegen.c: the dispatch (and dispatch_linked) code performs a 1-byte out-of-bounds read from a heap buffer during bytecode generation/dispatch. A crafted input can trigger this OOB read, leading to crashes, undefined behavior or potential information disclosure.

A heap-buffer-overflow occurs in mrb_ary_splice (src/array.c), where value_move (src/value_array.h) performs an out-of-bounds read (8 bytes past a heap-allocated array) during array splice/assignment (mrb_ary_aset). This can cause heap memory corruption, crashes, or potentially enable arbitrary code execution.

Heap-use-after-free in mruby's VM stack handling: mrb_funcall_with_block (src/vm.c) / related stack copy logic can read from freed VM stack memory (observed during calls such as mrb_instance_new / mrb_make_exception). This use-after-free can cause interpreter crashes, undefined behavior or memory corruption and may be exploitable with crafted input.

Heap-use-after-free in mruby-bigint: mpz_init_set_str (mrbgems/mruby-bigint/core/bigint.c), invoked via mrb_bint_new_str, can read from freed or otherwise invalid heap memory when initializing a BigInt from a string. This results in a crash (SEGV) and potential memory corruption, with possible denial-of-service or further exploitation.

A heap-buffer-overflow (out-of-bounds read) exists in mpz_get_int (mrbgems/mruby-bigint/core/bigint.c): the function can read past the allocated bigint limb array (e.g. accessing y->p[1] beyond the allocation). This can be triggered during bigint comparisons (mrb_bint_cmp / num_gt) and may lead to crashes or other undefined behavior.

An index-out-of-bounds write in mruby's pack/unpack handling: malformed pack templates can cause unpack_hex / pack_unpack (mrbgems/mruby-pack/src/pack.c) to drive string creation with an incorrect size, leading to an out-of-bounds write in str_new -> str_init_embed (src/mruby/src/string.c). This can crash the process (SIGSEGV) and cause memory corruption, potentially enabling further exploitation.

A heap-buffer-overflow in src/string.c's mrb_memsearch_ss: the function performs an 8-byte out-of-bounds read past a heap-allocated string buffer while performing substring search/split (seen via mrb_memsearch / mrb_str_split_m). This can lead to crashes or information disclosure/other undefined behavior during string search/split operations.

Heap-buffer-overflow (out-of-bounds read) in memsearch_swar (src/string.c): during substring search the code can invoke memcmp past the end of the target buffer, causing reads beyond the allocated heap. This issue is reachable via mrb_memsearch / mrb_str_index / str_convert_range / mrb_str_aref and can lead to crashes or potential heap memory disclosure.

Heap-use-after-free in the mruby VM (mrb_vm_exec in src/vm.c). During certain VM execution paths (involving cipush/mrb_ary_splat and nested mrb_vm_exec calls) an object is reallocated/freed (mrb_realloc/mrb_realloc_simple) while still referenced by the VM, and the VM later reads from that freed heap memory. This can cause crashes and undefined behavior, and may enable memory corruption or further exploitation with crafted inputs.

Heap-use-after-free in MuPDF's PDF object resolution path (seen in pdf_cache_object -> pdf_resolve_indirect -> pdf_resolve_indirect_chain). While resolving indirect objects the code accesses/writes memory that has already been freed, leading to heap corruption and crashes and potentially enabling further exploitation.

Heap-buffer-overflow in generic_unpack (src/lib/OpenEXRCore/unpack.c): while unpacking/decoding image data (via exr_decoding_run / readCoreScanlinePart), generic_unpack performs an out-of-bounds read of 4 bytes past a heap-allocated buffer. This insufficient bounds checking / incorrect buffer sizing can cause crashes, memory corruption and may enable information disclosure or further exploitation when parsing crafted OpenEXR files.

A heap-buffer-overflow (out-of-bounds read) occurs in src/lib/OpenEXRCore/internal_huf.c: the fasthuf_read_bits routine (invoked from fasthuf_initialize during Huffman table parsing and used by internal_huf_decompress / internal_exr_undo_piz) can read past the end of the input buffer when processing malformed or truncated Huffman table data. This can cause crashes or potential information disclosure during decompression.

A heap-buffer-overflow (out-of-bounds read) occurs during DWA decompression: while parsing compressed DWA blocks in DwaCompressor_uncompress (internal_dwa_compressor.h) via exr_uncompress_buffer and libdeflate_zlib_decompress_ex, a 16-bit unaligned read (get_unaligned_be16/load_u16_unaligned) can read two bytes past the end of the input buffer for malformed compressed data. This can crash the process (DoS) and may lead to information disclosure or further memory corruption when processing crafted EXR files.

php_fgetcsv in ext/standard/file.c (invoked via zif_str_getcsv) can compute an incorrect copy length and pass a negative size to memcpy (ASAN negative-size-param). This leads to an invalid memcpy call that can cause memory corruption/heap overflow and crashes when parsing specially crafted CSV input, potentially enabling denial-of-service or other memory-safety issues.

Heap-buffer-overflow (out-of-bounds read) in PackMachBase::canUnpack (p_mach.cpp) via get_ne32/get_le32 (bele.h). While iterating Mach-O load commands (including fat/32-bit paths), a malformed or too-short command can cause a 4-byte read past the allocated buffer, leading to crashes and possible disclosure of heap memory.

Stack-buffer-overflow in PackLinuxElf64::unpack (src/p_lx_elf.cpp): when locating a b_info structure inside a local peek buffer the code computes an offset and performs a 4-byte read (via get_le32/get_ne32) without ensuring the offset + sizeof(b_info) fits inside the buffer. A crafted packed ELF can trigger an out‑of‑bounds read on the stack, causing crashes and potential information disclosure or other undefined behavior.

Heap-buffer-overflow in PackLinuxElf64::unpack (p_lx_elf.cpp). While unpacking ELF data, N_BELE_RTP::LEPolicy::get64 / get_le64 (bele_policy.h / bele.h) can read an 8-byte little-endian value past the end of a MemBuffer allocation, due to insufficient bounds validation of ELF header/segment data. This out-of-bounds read can cause crashes and may lead to information disclosure when processing malformed ELF files.

Heap-buffer-overflow (out-of-bounds read) in PackLinuxElf32::elf_lookup (src/p_lx_elf.cpp). While walking ELF DT_HASH chains to resolve symbols the code can index past the end of the chains table and invoke a 32-bit read (via the get32/get_le32 path), causing a 4-byte heap OOB read. A malformed or malicious DT_HASH can therefore trigger crashes and potential information disclosure.

A global-buffer-overflow in m3_compile.c: Compile_BlockStatements (opcode decoding) causes an out-of-bounds read from the global opcode table c_operationsFC. While compiling/parsing block expressions (seen via Parse_InitExpr / ParseSection_Data), an opcode index can exceed the c_operationsFC bounds and read 8 bytes past the array, leading to crashes or disclosure of adjacent memory.

An out of bounds read occurs when searching for the tag message during tag parsing. The code uses `strstr(buffer, "\n\n")` to locate the separator between tag fields and the tag message, but since `strstr` does not accept a buffer length, it may read past the end of the buffer. This can result in `strstr` returning a pointer outside the buffer, causing the subsequent calculation of `buffer_end - buffer` to overflow and potentially lead to an invalid memory allocation.

The MMR decoder in jbig2dec pre-buffers up to 32 bits of encoded input data in a word buffer before consumption. When refilling the buffer, the decoder avoids reading data from succeeding segments but still reports having consumed those bytes, even though they were never read. After finishing, the MMR decoder propagates an incorrect number of consumed bytes to the caller. The caller then subtracts this incorrect value from the size, leading to an underflow. This causes subsequent MMR decoding to read input data from the wrong location and eventually attempt to read outside the MMR encoded input buffer.

A vulnerability exists in the attributes code where uninitialized memory is freed, potentially leading to undefined behavior.

stb_image does not reject fractional JPEG component subsampling ratios. The component resamplers are not written to support this, and such ratios can appear in crafted JPEG files, leading to potential issues.

A vulnerability exists in json_tokener where a utf8_replacement_char is unnecessarily added if input runs out in the middle of a unicode escape within the json_tokener_state_escape_unicode case, potentially leading to incorrect handling of incomplete unicode sequences.

A heap overflow vulnerability exists in cfgparse due to incorrect handling of empty lines. Specifically, on an empty line, the variable end equals line, which allows dereferencing end-1 without ensuring that end is greater than line, leading to unsafe memory access when checking for a trailing LF. This issue is present only in version 2.2.

A heap out of bounds read occurs in JSLexer::consumeBracedCodePoint due to continued use of the curCharPtr_ pointer after it is set to the end of the buffer. This situation arises when an invalid code point triggers a call to forceEOF in JSLexer::error, which sets curCharPtr_ to the buffer's end, but JSLexer::consumeBracedCodePoint does not properly handle this state and reads past the buffer boundary.
An out-of-bounds read occurs in code fence detection.

A vulnerability exists in the URI scope parsing code in guri, where the parser can read past the end of a URI if it encounters an incorrect %-escaped character. This issue affects the handling of zone ID syntax as defined in RFC 6874, which amends RFC 3986. The vulnerability also impacts the correctness of network-address tests related to zone IDs.
